name: Composition–dispersion experiments
summary: Otto Schott and Ernst Abbe melted trial glasses and measured how each composition bent and spread light, learning which ingredients gave the optical properties lens makers needed.
description: Schott and Abbe, with Zeiss workshop cooperation, measured experimental glass melts spectrometrically to relate composition to refractive and dispersive properties and select further compositions.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.
why: Abbe's lens designs called for glasses with combinations of refraction and dispersion that existing glassworks did not make.
